clue.text: Doles out insulting remarks, hiding compliments

indicators.note: whatever hides something keeps it out of sight inside itself, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: to diss is slang for to insult; a diss is an insulting remark
a tribute is a compliment or expression of praise

explanation.surface: Someone hands out insults while holding back any praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding compliments' reads as withholding praise, but it is the container signal. Diss is modern slang for insult; the plural 'compliments' is loose, read as praise in general.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to hand or share out, exactly as charity or rations are doled out to recipients.

clue.text: In bed, upset and down, there's Everyman, lacking spine etc

indicators.note: something that is in another thing is placed inside it, so one piece sits within the other
to upset is to tip over, so in a vertical entry the letters are turned bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned over
D is the standard abbreviation for down, as in crossword clue numbers
everyman is the ordinary person, the generic 'one'; also the setter's own name

explanation.surface: A miserable person lies in bed feeling low and spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset is read literally as turned upside down, and D is the usual crossword shorthand for down. Everyman is the setter's own name and also the ordinary person, 'one'. 'Lacking spine' reads as feeble, but it is a fish with its backbone removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deboned describes fish or meat with its bones taken out, so it lacks a spine and the rest of its skeleton.

clue.text: Son to strip off warm-weather wear

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
to strip off is to take your clothes off

explanation.surface: A boy peels off his clothes on a hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: S for son plus UNDRESS for strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundress is a light, sleeveless dress worn in hot sunny weather, so it is clothing for summer.

clue.text: Heading off in wide thoroughfare

indicators.note: with the heading off, the first letter at the top is removed

parts.note: broad means wide

explanation.surface: Someone sets off along a broad avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: BROAD loses its first letter. 'Heading off' reads as setting off on a journey, but it means beheading the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a public way for traffic, and a road is the commonest kind of such route.

clue.text: Performing Schubert: Trout and Alleluja's openings providing something to chew on?

indicators.note: a performance is an interpretation, so these letters are played in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so only the first letters are wanted

parts.note: first letters of the two titles

explanation.surface: A concert of Schubert's Trout quintet and Mozart's Alleluja gives the audience food for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic titles look like the programme, but only their initials count, joining SCHUBERT as anagram fodder. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruschetta is Italian toasted bread with toppings, literally food to bite and chew, punning on 'something to chew on' as a thought.

clue.text: Comeuppance for a bounder having stolen one item belonging to princess

indicators.note: a comeuppance read literally is a coming up, so in a down clue the letters rise from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what has stolen something holds it inside, so one piece is taken in by another

parts.note: a bounder is a cad or rotter, a rat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cad who pinched a princess's jewel finally gets what he deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAT goes up to give TARA, which then takes in I. 'Comeuppance' is a lovely reversal signal: literally coming up the grid. Bounder is old British slang for a dishonourable man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental crown or headband, worn classically by princesses at formal occasions.

clue.text: Digression following home counties coast

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the first-named part goes second

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE
an aside is a digression from the main subject

explanation.surface: A rambling tangent leads from the Home Counties down to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties around London, all in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coast considered as a place for holidays, beaches and promenades by the water.

clue.text: Thrifty shopper unearthing bra, pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are nonsense needing rearranging

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A frugal shopper rummages through the sale bins for underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like more underwear beside 'bra', but in British slang it means rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain hunter seeks goods at low prices, which is what a thrifty, money-saving customer does.

clue.text: Touring Greece, playing instrument

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A musician tours Greece, performing on their instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing instrument' suggests music, but the instrument is a scientific one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Geiger counter is a scientific device that detects and measures radiation, so it is a measuring instrument.

clue.text: Primarily, Arnauts' land; Balkan; Adriatic notably; Ionian additionally!

definitions.text: Primarily, Arnauts' land; Balkan; Adriatic notably; Ionian additionally!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letters are taken

parts.words: Arnauts' land; Balkan; Adriatic notably; Ionian additionally
parts.note: first letters of the seven words

explanation.surface: A gazetteer entry: home of the Arnauts, a Balkan state on the Adriatic and Ionian seas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition. Arnauts is an old Turkish name for Albanians.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a Balkan country whose coastline faces both the Adriatic and the Ionian seas, home of the Arnauts.

clue.text: A conflict between UN and Spain is unenlightened

indicators.note: what lies between two things has them on either side, so it is enclosed

parts.note: taken as written
a conflict is a war
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A war between the United Nations and Spain shows someone is clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: UN and E sit either side of A WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unenlightened means lacking knowledge or information, which is to be ignorant or uninformed of something.

clue.text: King George welcoming a toast

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
a means one

explanation.surface: The king welcomes guests with a raised glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like a drink to the king's health, but slang 'you're toast' means you are finished.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang someone who is toast is doomed or done for, and a goner is a person beyond saving.

clue.text: Scratching nail into neck

indicators.note: to go into something is to enter it, ending up inside

parts.note: scrag is the neck of mutton, a British cut of meat
a pin is a small nail-like fastener

explanation.surface: A fingernail scratches someone's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nail' suggests a fingernail but is a PIN; scrag is a cheap British cut, the scrawny neck of mutton, and also slang for a neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraping and scratching both mean drawing something rough or sharp across a surface, as near synonyms.

clue.text: Titled lord recollected the animals were his friends

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the character

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again, so the letters are reassembled in another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An aristocrat reminisces that his animals were his companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but split as re-collected it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Dolittle, Hugh Lofting's fictional physician, could talk with creatures and preferred their company to people's.

clue.text: Popular recording about alien life form is giving too much away

parts.note: what is in is fashionable and popular
a disc is a record
re means about, concerning
ET, the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: A hit record about an alien reveals too many secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it wraps something round, but it is simply RE in the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indiscreet talks without care, revealing secrets or private matters others would keep quiet.

clue.text: Tolerate a beast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put up with, endure
second meaning: a large furry animal

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a verb of enduring and the name of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means endure or put up with; as a noun it names a large heavy mammal.

clue.text: A stinker finally strove to aspire to ascend in scholarly life

parts.note: taken as written
a stinker is a nasty person, a cad

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means climbing upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: to aspire is to aim

explanation.surface: A rotter at last tries to climb the academic ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: AIM goes upward to MIA at the end. 'To ascend in scholarly life' reads as one phrase, but 'in' separates the reversal signal from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities, research and scholarship, the environment of academic careers.

clue.text: Intact, we're told: there's a gap!

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: intact means complete, in one piece

explanation.surface: Something claimed to be undamaged turns out to have an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the two sound-alike words are near opposites: complete, and with a piece missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole is an opening or empty space in something, just as a gap is a break or space.

clue.text: Museum director's in arrangement with boards

parts.note: the Louvre is the great Paris museum
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A gallery director sits in a meeting with the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boards' suggests a company board, but here they are wooden slats.
explanation.definitionFit: Louvred means fitted with louvres, angled overlapping slats letting air in, like shutters on a window.

clue.text: British field marshal and Mexican artist in conversation in upscale resort

indicators.note: in conversation words are spoken, so their sound is what counts

parts.note: Monty was the nickname of Field Marshal Montgomery
Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter

explanation.surface: Montgomery and Frida Kahlo chat together at a fashionable resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Montgomery led British forces at El Alamein and was nicknamed Monty; Frida Kahlo is the famous Mexican painter. Said aloud together they give the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo is the glamorous district of Monaco, famed for its casino, yachts and wealthy visitors.

clue.text: Royals are beheaded, chaps

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, the first letter

parts.note: the word loses its first letter
gents are gentlemen, chaps

explanation.surface: Royal men are executed, like Charles I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royals are beheaded' reads as a grim headline, but 'Royals' is the definition and 'are' is the word being beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Regents rule in place of an underage or absent monarch, so they wield royal power, loosely royals.

clue.text: Anxious card player with twitch hiding money

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it out of sight inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: North is one of the four players in bridge
a tic is a nervous twitch
the euro is a currency

explanation.surface: A nervous gambler with a twitch is hiding cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are named North, South, East and West, so a card player can be N; N and TIC together hold EURO.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic describes someone prone to excessive worry and nervous tension, close in sense to anxious.

clue.text: Poem concerning classical theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A verse written about an ancient playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is also a British cinema chain, but here it is the ancient building.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome an odeon was a roofed building for music and recitals, a kind of playhouse.

clue.text: Oddly ignored odour before booze consumed with gusto

indicators.note: what comes before is placed first, ahead of what follows
ignoring the odd-placed letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: second and fourth letters
gin is a type of booze

explanation.surface: A drinker ignores the smell and knocks back the liquor enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'strangely', but it means the odd letters, which are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is an informal idiom for starting to eat heartily, so dug in means ate eagerly.

clue.text: Cunning aspect of anarchosyndicalism

indicators.note: an aspect of something is a part of it, so the letters lie within

parts.note: letters three to six

explanation.surface: Political scheming is a feature of radical left-wing movements.
explanation.walkthrough: Anarchosyndicalism is a movement for worker-run trade unions; the answer sits inside its opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means knowing, sly or mischievously clever, as in an arch look, so it means crafty.

clue.text: Not having fun seeing some letters in Learn Estonian

indicators.note: only some of the letters within the title are taken, a run lying inside it

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Studying a textbook called Learn Estonian is joyless work.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title looks like a real book, but its run of letters across the word break is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and solemn in manner, the opposite of light-hearted play and amusement.

clue.text: French perhaps fabricated accounts of love

definitions.note: adjective, as in a Romance language
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a language descended from Latin, of which French is one

explanation.surface: The French, perhaps, make up love stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like the nation's reputation for love, but it is an example of a language family.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance languages descend from Latin, French among them; a romance is also a fictional tale of love.

clue.text: In the end, England falling short with runs: idiots!

indicators.note: at the end means the last position, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word
what falls short comes in under the mark
to run an organisation is to head it

explanation.surface: A cricket fan despairs as England fall short of their target in runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like cricket scoring, but it is a verb, as in runs a company. 'In the end' reads as eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunderhead is an old-fashioned word for a stupid person, a blockhead or fool.
